abstract:
Reliable biomarkers for predicting neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) response in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) remain limited. We explored whether RecurIndex-derived molecular features were associated with total pathological complete response (tpCR).
Seventy-four patients with TNBC treated with dose-dense NAC were analyzed. Associations between RecurIndex risk scores, 18 core genes, and tpCR were assessed using logistic regression and ROC analyses. Clinical-molecular models were internally validated by bootstrap resampling. Public single-cell RNA-seq data were used for biological contextualization.
Twenty-nine patients (39.2%) achieved tpCR. The distant recurrence score, was significantly associated with tpCR. OBSL1, BLM, and CCR1 were identified as candidate tpCR-associated genes. The model combining OBSL1, BLM, and clinical nodal stage achieved an AUC of 0.838 and an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.799.
RecurIndex-derived molecular features were associated with tpCR in TNBC. These exploratory findings warrant validation in independent cohorts.
